mostWorthwhile.text: Using the spindle on the copied DNA was most worthwhile: the planned time-strip connects chromosome separation to two complete nuclei while showing that the cytoplasm is still connected.

leastWorthwhile.text: Copying the DNA felt comparatively abbreviated. The result shows sister chromatids but gives little sense of how nucleotide pairing copies the strands.

surprise.text: The spindle is presented as a preview of assembly during mitosis, clarifying its timing after DNA copying rather than implying it was already attached to chromosomes.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless: each was tied to a stated goal. The jump from general new cell proteins to spindle fibres was less explicit until the result identified tubulin.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the constructions connect cell growth and division clearly, and the later paths toward different cell types offer a question worth following.
